english: Who are you, man? I am your brother-in-law (husband's brother). Young woman, wife, be dear to us. Where is my husband? He is in the field, he plows, and in the evening he will come back. I am hungry and thirsty. Sit, eat this meat and milk, and drink. Our mother cooked this for you. Your mother is dear to me.
uncertain: h₂yúHn̥ḱa nos gʷḗn: vocative 'young wife' with nos read as 'to us'
last line: whose mother is meant

english: Mother, I am bringing home a young wife. -- Your father died; I am a widow and the hearth grows cold. -- She will warm the house for us. -- Who is she? -- She is the daughter of the kindly shepherd. -- I know her; she weaves beautiful clothes. Bring her to me; I love her. -- Mother, you will not be alone.
uncertain: h₁íh₂m̥ moy wédʰe: 'bring her to me' vs 'marry her for me'

english: Grandmother, may I come in? -- Young wife, come in and praise the fire of our hearth. -- How do I praise it? -- Say: 'Fire, protect this house and give us children. Fire, protect this house and give us children.' -- Now the fire knows you. Sit by the fire and eat.
uncertain: h₂Hséh₂s read as gen. 'of the hearth'
ph₂wéni read as locative 'by the fire'

english: Brother, why are you taking my horse? -- I am not taking it; father gave it to me. -- You are lying to me. -- Father gave it to me last year. -- Brother, do not be angry. Let us two not fight. Let us now ask father; he is wise and will judge between us. -- Now ride it, and I will drive the cows. Brother, you are dear to me.
uncertain: nos méǵʰye: 'to us, to me' doubled dative unclear

english: Husband, do you remember the day when you led me to your house? -- I remember it. You wore a bright garment and your brothers sang through the night. -- We two have lived many years. Sons grew up for us, and our daughters have gone to far-off villages. Are you sad? -- I am not sad; you are with me.
uncertain: dweh₂róns ḱóymons 'to far villages' (acc. of goal)

english: Sister, a young man gave me a ring. -- Who gave it? -- The son of the shepherd rich in horses. I am older than you. The elder goes first. Now look for a husband quickly. -- Yesterday I saw the shepherd's brother. -- Then let the two of us be wed on the same day. May the gods give us good husbands.
